content:
Frailty is a state where the body has less reserve to cope with illness or change. Arthritis can contribute through pain, reduced activity and muscle loss.

This guide explains what frailty services can offer and how to access them. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What frailty services can offer

  • A comprehensive geriatric assessment.
  • A medicines review.
  • Falls assessment and strength and balance support.
  • Help planning care and support.

England

GP practices identify frailty and can refer you to community or hospital frailty services. Ask your GP what is available locally.

Wales

Health boards provide community and hospital frailty services. Ask your GP or local health board.

Scotland

Health and social care partnerships provide frailty support. Ask your GP practice.

Northern Ireland

Health and Social Care Trusts provide services for older people. Ask your GP or trust.

How this fits with arthritis care

Frailty services work alongside your GP, rheumatology team or physiotherapist. Share your arthritis diagnosis and treatment.

Making the most of an appointment

  • Bring a list of medicines.
  • Note what matters most to you.
  • Bring a family member or carer if helpful.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Does frailty mean I am getting worse?

Not necessarily. Frailty can improve with the right support.

Can I refer myself?

Usually not. Ask your GP.

If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
